FREEDOM WITH BOUNDARIES

Give your agent room to work.
Start with a secure environment.

Execution, credentials, and permissions. Each in its place.

01

A workspace of its own

Your agent and its tools run in an isolated environment inside a local virtual machine, without gaining access to your entire host.

ISOLATED BY DESIGN
02

Access without the keys

The environment holds your account credentials separately. Your agent uses resources through controlled interfaces, without credentials entering its workspace.

CREDENTIALS STAY SEPARATE
03

You choose the access

Choose which folders and accounts to make available. Connected accounts use standing authorization by default, with optional per-request approval. You can revoke access.

ACCESS ON YOUR TERMS

A FEW THINGS TO KNOW

Before you begin.

Read the security model ↗
Can I use Anchi today?+

Anchi is an open-source developer preview. A security audit, formal signed-artifact validation, and public distribution are not yet complete. macOS on Apple Silicon is supported; Linux support is experimental. Follow the getting started guide to set it up.

Does local execution mean my data stays on my computer?+

No. Content your agent reads may be sent to cloud models. Anchi isolates credentials from the agent, but cannot prevent every prompt injection or misuse of an authorized interface. It is not suitable for unattended processing of sensitive real accounts.

Do I need to approve every action?+

No. Account connectors and model calls use standing authorization by default, with an option for per-request approval. Tool calls inside the isolated environment and file operations in granted folders do not prompt for individual approval. Folder grants last until revoked.

Which resources can I connect?+

Gmail (read-only), Google Drive, Notion, Slack, and host folder access are implemented. Real-account validation for Drive, Notion, and Slack is still incomplete. The current runtime uses Pi with Codex subscription authentication. Multiple agent instances are not yet supported.
